  • Creates a new fundamental law that defines the Québec nation and its collective rights.
  • States that this law overrides any other inconsistent rule.
  • Includes human rights and freedoms and language rights as part of the Constitution.

  • Removes the sections on the former Legislative Council of Québec, which no longer exists.

Part 8 Code of Civil Procedure

  • Adds mandatory information to the public roll of members of each professional order.
  • Changes the minimum number of member signatures required to request a special general meeting.
  • Allows people holding a psychotherapist permit obtained elsewhere in Canada to practise psychotherapy in Québec, under rules set by the Office.

  • Nurses will be able to start examinations and tests in more situations, not only for public health reasons.
  • They will also be able to prescribe examinations, tests, medications, other substances, products, and dressings, under upcoming rules.
  • Removes the rule limiting voting rights at general meetings to section delegates only.
Part 3 Midwives Act
  • Midwives will be able to prescribe and provide more types of contraception.
  • They will be able to screen more broadly for sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections.
  • They will be able to treat these infections in a person without symptoms if their screening test is positive.

  • An act can be considered the practice of the profession even if it is not done for payment.

  • Marriage and family therapists will be able to practise psychotherapy without a special permit, like psychologists and physicians.
  • The Office des professions will be able to authorize students to carry out certain psychotherapist activities during their training.

  • The Québec Cabinet will be able to set cases where a pharmacist may prescribe or substitute a medication with a product made by a company in which they have a financial interest.

  • A new rule will allow a drug manufacturer to pay certain benefits to an intermediary, such as a pharmacy banner or chain.
